title: Calcified lung + splenic lesions (Ohio): histoplasmosis
vignette: A 46-year-old, previously healthy man develops sudden-onset, sharp, left-sided flank pain radiating to the groin. CT scan of the abdomen reveals a left ureteral calculus, which he passes spontaneously in the urine. Other, incidental findings include a left lower lobe lung nodule and foci of calcifications in the spleen. Chest imaging shows several small calcified nodules in both lungs and a calcified mediastinal lymph node. The patient has had no pulmonary symptoms and is a lifelong nonsmoker. He is a farmer who lives in Ohio and has not traveled recently. Tuberculosis skin test shows a <5 mm induration at 48 hours. Repeat chest imaging 3 months later reveals no changes. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the observed findings in this patient?

clues.text: foci of calcifications in the spleen
clues.note: Calcified splenic lesions (plus calcified lung/lymph nodes) reflect an old, contained granulomatous infection that spread via the reticuloendothelial system - classic for histoplasmosis.

clues.text: a farmer who lives in Ohio
clues.note: The Ohio (and Mississippi) River Valley is the endemic region for Histoplasma capsulatum (soil/bird-bat droppings) - a strong geographic clue.

clues.text: Tuberculosis skin test shows a <5 mm induration
clues.note: A NEGATIVE tuberculin test argues against TB, favoring another granulomatous cause (histoplasmosis) of the calcified lesions.

clues.text: Repeat chest imaging 3 months later reveals no changes
clues.note: STABLE (unchanging), calcified nodules over time indicate a benign, contained granulomatous process (old fungal infection), not malignancy.

whatMatters: Multiple STABLE, CALCIFIED lung nodules + calcified mediastinal node + splenic calcifications in an asymptomatic Ohio-valley farmer with a NEGATIVE TB test = old, contained HISTOPLASMOSIS (a FUNGAL infection, Histoplasma capsulatum). Answer A. The organism spreads from lungs to the reticuloendothelial system (spleen/liver) and calcifies within granulomas.
strategy: Combine the geography (Ohio/Mississippi valley), calcified lung + SPLENIC lesions, negative TB test, and stability over time to reach histoplasmosis (contained granulomas). Reject metastatic cancer (lesions enlarge, calcification rare), miliary TB (ill/febrile, positive TB test, Ranke complex differs), parathyroid adenoma (hypercalcemia, doesn't seed lungs/spleen), and silica exposure (occupational upper-lobe nodular fibrosis, not splenic calcification/negative here).

eliminations.label: Metastatic cancer - lesions enlarge, calcification rare
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: multiple lung lesions from metastatic malignancy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: metastases generally ENLARGE over time and rarely calcify; these lesions are stable and calcified, and there's no primary tumor. ✅ Correct if: enlarging, noncalcified lung nodules with a known primary.

eliminations.label: Miliary tuberculosis - ill/febrile, positive TB test
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hematogenous TB with innumerable small lung nodules. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: patients are clinically ill (fever, night sweats), the TB skin test would be positive, and calcified lesions with a NEGATIVE test point away from TB. ✅ Correct if: systemic illness with a positive TB test/Ghon-Ranke complex.

eliminations.label: Parathyroid adenoma - hypercalcemia, not lung/spleen seeding
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a benign tumor causing primary hyperparathyroidism/hypercalcemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not spread to the lungs/spleen; metastatic calcification is rare and would come with systemic hypercalcemia signs. ✅ Correct if: hypercalcemia with high PTH.

eliminations.label: Silica exposure - occupational fibrosis, not splenic calcification (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: silicosis - inhaled silica causing upper-lobe nodular fibrosis (and 'eggshell' hilar node calcification) in miners/sandblasters. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this farmer's picture (splenic calcifications, calcified nodules from a disseminated granulomatous infection, endemic geography, negative TB test) fits histoplasmosis, not occupational silica. ✅ Correct if: an occupational silica-exposed worker with upper-lobe fibrotic nodules/eggshell calcification.

reasoning: Stable, calcified lung nodules + calcified mediastinal node + SPLENIC calcifications in an asymptomatic Ohio farmer
Negative TB test and unchanged imaging over 3 months indicate an old, contained granulomatous infection
Histoplasma (Ohio/Mississippi valley) spreads from lungs to the reticuloendothelial system and calcifies within granulomas
mechanism: Histoplasma capsulatum is a DIMORPHIC fungus endemic to the OHIO and Mississippi River Valleys, found in soil enriched with bird/bat droppings (farmers, cave explorers). Inhaled spores convert to the yeast form in the lungs and are PHAGOCYTOSED by alveolar macrophages; the fungus initially resists killing and can REPLICATE WITHIN macrophages, spreading through the draining LYMPHATICS and the RETICULOENDOTHELIAL SYSTEM (mediastinal nodes, SPLEEN, liver). After ~2 weeks, an intact host develops a cell-mediated immune response that CONTAINS the infection within GRANULOMAS, which over time FIBROSE and CALCIFY at the initial sites - producing the incidentally discovered, STABLE, calcified lung nodules, calcified mediastinal lymph node, and SPLENIC calcifications seen here. Most immunocompetent people are asymptomatic (a minority have a self-limited pneumonia). The negative tuberculin test and unchanged 3-month imaging support a benign, contained fungal process rather than TB, malignancy, or occupational disease. The distractors don't fit: metastases enlarge (rarely calcify), miliary TB causes illness with a positive test, parathyroid adenoma causes hypercalcemia (not lung/spleen lesions), and silicosis is an occupational upper-lobe fibrotic process without splenic calcification.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > histoplasmosis: Ohio/Mississippi valley, bird/bat droppings; intracellular (macrophage) replication; spreads to reticuloendothelial system; calcified lung + splenic granulomas; usually asymptomatic.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Stable calcified lung + splenic lesions + endemic exposure + negative TB = old histoplasmosis (fungal).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Histoplasma, dimorphic fungus, granuloma calcification, reticuloendothelial system, or silicosis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Metastasis (enlarges), miliary TB (ill/positive test), parathyroid adenoma (hypercalcemia), silicosis (occupational upper-lobe) don't fit calcified splenic lesions.
